propositions: A transient git fetch hang from the GitHub mirror times out at 300s and is converted to SnapshotFetchError, which the adapter's exception handler misclassifies as a review conclusion rather than infrastructure fault.
The adapter returns BLOCK with review-error reason for any exception, causing the voter to POST a durable -1 vote instead of abstaining.
The -1 vote removes the change from backfill reconciliation eligibility because reconcile.py pre-filters on already_voted and has_llm_review_vote, preventing re-review safety.
Infrastructure timeouts must be distinguished from genuine review conclusions and routed to the no-vote path that already exists for hung reviews at higher layers.

A retryable infrastructure fault (SnapshotFetchError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired, TimeoutError, ConnectionError) should result in ABSTAIN with no vote and no dedup row, leaving the change eligible for backfill retry.
